messages:
maria: Heads-up — received an escalation from Acme (enterprise). After the canary rollout this morning some transactional emails from the Generation API contained the previous customer's name ("OldCo") instead of the current customer's name. Customer is worried about data bleed.

jordan: Can you paste the request_id(s) and a short repro? Need timestamps to trace through logs.

maria: request_id=req_0a9f3b2c, time=2026-03-15T02:14:23Z. Repro steps from customer: 1) send prompt with prefix: "Dear {{company_name}}," where company_name=Acme; 2) immediate subsequent request with company_name=BetaInc; 3) BetaInc email came back: "Dear OldCo,". Attached logs:
```
2026-03-15T02:14:23Z req=req_0a9f3b2c route=acme model=redwood-v1.4 prefix_key=prefix-5f3a...
2026-03-15T02:14:23Z kv_cache HIT -> key=prefix-5f3a value=<<kv:template:OldCo>>
2026-03-15T02:14:23Z req=req_0a9f4d8e route=beta model=redwood-v1.4 prefix_key=prefix-5f3a...
2026-03-15T02:14:23Z kv_cache HIT -> key=prefix-5f3a value=<<kv:template:OldCo>>
```

maria: Customer says this happened for multiple users and is reproducing 3/10 times in their load tests. They paused traffic and want a mitigation and root cause.

sanjay: Looking at the canary notes — we landed "kv-prefix-key-optimization" which changed the key format to sha1(prompt) only. I suspect the key no longer includes route_id or model_version, so prefixes collide across customers. Grep from runtime logs shows: 
```
kv_key_v2 = sha1(prefix_text)
# old: kv_key = sha1(prefix_text + route_id + model_ver)
```

deploy-bot: Canary rollout "kv-prefix-key-optimization" -> started 2026-03-15T02:00Z, targets: hosted API, 10% traffic.

jordan: This is high severity (PII risk). Temporary mitigation options: 1) flush affected kv keys for Acme/Beta (fast), 2) route Acme to redwood-v1.3 until we ship a fix (zero code change), 3) increase canary rollback to 0%. Which do we want to do now?

maria: Customer asked to flush caches and have us roll traffic back if there's any chance of bleed. Please do flush now and route them to v1.3 while we triage. :exclamation:

ops-oncall: Running flush now -> `rcli kv flush --match "prefix-*5f3a*" --region=us-east-1`
ops-oncall: Result: 23 keys deleted, 0 failures.
ops-oncall: Applying route override for account acme -> `set-route --account=acme --model=redwood-v1.3 --temp-ttl=2h`
ops-oncall: Route update succeeded, traffic shifted.

maria: Customer confirms after flush + routing the responses look correct in their test. They still want root cause and a durable fix.

sanjay: Root cause summary: new keying removed route/account scoping from prefix keys, causing KV collisions between tenants when identical prefix text was used. Impact is stale templates / context appearing in subsequent requests. Proposed fix: restore explicit key components (route_id/account_id/model_version) in the prefix key and add a short randomized salt for safety. Patch sketch: 
```diff
- kv_key_v2 = sha1(prefix_text)
+ kv_key_v2 = sha1(prefix_text + "::" + route_id + "::" + model_version + "::" + account_id)
```
Also add a migration that treats old keys as cold misses (no automatic reuse).

jordan: Agree. Need a hotfix on the runtime (v1.4) and a backport to 1.3 branch to avoid surprises during future rollouts. Estimate: patch + tests ~4 hours, QA + canary ~2 hours. Schedule?

sanjay: I'll own the hotfix. Will PR in next 30m and tag @jordan for rollout. We'll also add an integration test that simulates interleaved requests from two accounts to prevent regressions.

maria: Thanks — I'll open a customer communication with timeline and confirm mitigations. Linking ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INFR-7892 to track.

jordan: Assigning INFR-7892 to sanjay, label: severity/P1, owner-oncall.

maria: Appreciate the quick response team. I'll keep CSM updated and paste customer confirmation here when they acknowledge closure. :white_check_mark:
